rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproach shifts from their dislike of truth to turning from the Qur’an, their worldly and otherworldly honor, which they ought to welcome fully.
rows.anchor: انتقال من تشنيعهم بكراهة الحق الذي يقوم به العالم إلى تشنيعهم بالأعراض عما جبل عليه كل نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their reminder” is the Qur’an, their honor and renown in both worlds; 43:44 likewise calls it a reminder for Muhammad and his people.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالذكر القرآن الذي فيه فخرهم وشرفهم في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Qur’an brings what reforms them now and remembrance in the hereafter, but by bad choice they turn from present well-being and their noble end.
rows.anchor: التأويلات النجمية" : {بل أتيناهم} بما فيه لهم صلاح في الحال

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad specifies that they turn away from their own particular pride and honor, rather than from things that merit no attention.
rows.anchor: الإرشاد" : أي فخرهم وشرفهم خاصة {معرضون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question turns from the rebuke over their claim that the Messenger was possessed to another rebuke: do they allege that he asks payment for his mission?
rows.anchor: انتقال من توبيخهم بما ذكر من قولهم أو يقولون به جنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharj means a payment or wage; the implication is that they refuse to believe because they imagine he seeks one.
rows.anchor: أي : جعلا وأجر فلأجل ذلك لا يؤمنون بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s provision in this life and reward in the next are broader and more lasting than their payment, leaving the Messenger independent of their gifts.
rows.anchor: فإن رزق ربك في الدنيا وثوابه في العقبى خير لك من ذلك لسعته ودوامه ففيه استغناء لك عن عطائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharj commonly means what one pays out to another; kharaj commonly denotes land tax, suggesting abundance and regularity, so it is the stronger term for God’s gift.
rows.anchor: والخرج بإزاء الدخل يقال لكل ما تخرجه إلى غيرك والخراج غالب في الضريبة على الأرض ففيه إشعار بالكثرة واللزوم

rows.speaker: تفسير المناسبات
rows.claim: The commentary says God calls it kharaj to signal that He has pledged each person’s provision to Himself with a promise He will not break.
rows.anchor: تفسير المناسبات" : وكأنه سماه خراجا إشارة إلى أنه أوجب رزق كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best giver of recompense for work because His gift neither ends nor becomes clouded; this explains the superiority of His provision.
rows.anchor: أي خير من أعطى عوضا على عمل لأن ما يعطيه لا ينقطع ولا يتكدر وهو تقدير لخيرية خراجه تعالى

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The firmly grounded knowers of God do not stain their luminous hearts with worldly or otherworldly desires while calling people to God through God.
rows.anchor: التأويلات النجمية" : فيه إشارة إلى أن العلماء بالله الراسخين في العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet warns that an exegete loses by selling knowledge and skill for bread, reinforcing the call to avoid payment-seeking.
rows.anchor: زيان ميكند مرد تفسير دان كه علم وهنر ميفر وشدبنان

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi’s position permits a preacher to take wages, among the most lawful earnings, though abstaining is better; prophets chose their reward from God rather than people.
rows.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره الأطهر في "الفتوحات المكية" : مذهبنا أن للواعظ أخذ الأجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound minds recognize the straightness of the path Muhammad calls them to; it has no crookedness that could justify accusing him.
rows.anchor: تشهد العقول السلمية باستقامة لا عوج فيه يوجب اتهامهم لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of the hereafter censures their absorption in worldly life and their claim that worldly life is the only life; “the path” refers to the straight path.
rows.anchor: وصفوا بذلك تشنيعا لهم بما هم عليه من الانهماك في الدنيا وزعمهم أن لا حياة إلا الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakibun means turning aside or deviating from the straight path; belief in the hereafter and fear of its terrors would strongly motivate seeking truth and following it.
rows.anchor: مائلون عادلون عنه فإن الإيمان بالآخرة وخوف ما فيها من الدواهي من أقوى الدواعي إلى طلب الحق

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says one who neglects the return and what will be shown about him in the highest assembly is astray and not rightly guided; better still is one unconcerned with his pre-eternal allotment.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : من لم يهتم لأمر معاده ومنقلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses show unbelievers are obstinate and refuted from every angle in their refusal to follow and listen to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ثم في الآيات إخبار أن الكفار متعنتون محجوجون من كل وجه في ترك الاتباع والاستماع إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdi’s poem portrays the heedless as unable to hear truth: knowledge bores them, admonition shames them, and rain cannot make flowers grow from stone.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره

rows.speaker: بهلول
rows.claim: In the reported encounter, Bahlul tells Harun that a ruler answers for oppression anywhere, and tests his state by Qur’anic judgments on deeds, kinship, and intercession.
rows.anchor: وقف بهلول المجنون على طريقة وناداه بأعلى صوته يا هارون ثلاثا

rows.speaker: بهلول
rows.claim: Bahlul refuses Harun’s offer to repay his debts or provide a pension: debt cannot be paid with debt, and God will not remember Harun while forgetting His other servant.
rows.anchor: الدين لا يقضى بدين أد أموال الناس إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bahlul’s final answer points to this verse: provision arriving unexpectedly from God is better than provision from a specified source.
rows.anchor: وأشار بهلول في قوله الأخير إلى مضمون قوله تعالى : {فخراج ربك خير}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs were recited to them in worldly life, and they denied them then.
rows.anchor: ألم تكن ءاياتى تتلى عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say their misery, acquired through their bad choices, mastered them and led their circumstances to an evil end.
rows.anchor: التي اقترفناها بسوء اختيارنا فصارت أحوالنا مؤدية إلى سوء العاقبة

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls the best explanation that their pleasures and desires overcame them; they are called misery because they lead to misery.
rows.anchor: القرطبي : وأحسن ما قيل في معناه غلبت علينا لذاتنا

rows.speaker: أبو تراب
rows.claim: Abu Turab defines misery as thinking well of oneself and thinking badly of other people.
rows.anchor: أبو تراب : الشقوة حسن الظن بالنفس وسوء الظن بالخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were astray from the truth, which explains their denial and their other sins.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فعلنا ما فعلنا من التكذيب وسائر المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They beg to be brought out of the Fire and promise that, if they return to sin, they will be wrongdoers who exceed the limit against themselves.
rows.anchor: متجاوزون الحد في الظلم لأنفسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine command humiliates them into silence and orders them to be driven back like dogs when scolded; khasaʾa means to be repelled.
rows.anchor: اسكتوا في النار سكوت هوان فإنها ليست مقام سؤال وانزجروا انزجار الكلاب إذا زجرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s immense generosity and mercy purify people of blameworthy traits despite their deserving punishment; He created them for mercy, while punishment follows their bad choices.
rows.anchor: غاية كرم الله ورحمته وفضله على عباده حيث يتفضل عليهم ويرحمهم ويزكيهم عن أوصافهم الذميمة مع استحقاقهم العذاب الأليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With damma, khutwah is the distance between the feet; with fatha, one stride. Following footsteps idiomatically means adopting someone’s way, here Satan’s course.
rows.anchor: جمع خطوة بضم الخاء وهي ما بين القدمين أي ما بين رجلي الخاطي وبالفتح المرة الواحدة من الخطو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must not follow paths Satan whispers into their hearts and beautifies to their eyes, including spreading or cherishing scandal.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا تسلكوا الطرق التي يدعوكم إليها الشيطان ويوسوس بها في قلوبكم ويزينها لأعينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fahshaʾ is what is extremely ugly by custom or reason, in word or deed; munkar is what the Law rejects, while Abu Layth says it is unknown to scripture and sunnah.
rows.anchor: والفحشاء والفاحشة ما عظم قبحه عرفا وعقلا سواء كان فعلا أو قولا والمنكر ما ينكره الشرع

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu Layth defines munkar as what is not recognized in a revealed law or the Sunna.
rows.anchor: أبو الليث : المنكر ما لا يعرف في شريعة ولا سنة

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat includes what sound reason deems ugly or leaves undecided, provided the Law judges it ugly.
rows.anchor: المفردات" : المنكر كل شيء تحكم العقول الصحيحة بقبحه أو تتوقف في استقباحه العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Satan’s beautifying and goading an “order” belittles the followers who heed him.
rows.anchor: واستعير الأمر لتزيينه وبعثه لهم على الشر تحقيرا لشأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor includes these explanations, enabling repentance that erases sins, and the institution of legal penalties that expiate them; without this, no one would be purified.
rows.anchor: بهذه البيانات والتوفيق للتوبة الماحية للذنوب وشرع الحدود المكفرة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In min kum min ahad, the first min is explanatory; the second is extra, and ahad is nominative as the subject.
rows.anchor: من الأولى بيانية والثانية زائدة واحد في حيز الرفع على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abadan means for all time, without end.
rows.anchor: آخر الدهر لا إلى نهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God purifies whom He wills by bestowing the effects of grace and mercy, guiding the person to repentance and accepting it, as He did for them.
rows.anchor: من عباده بإفاضة آثار فضله ورحمته عليه وحمله على التوبة ثم قبولها منه كما فعل بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the Qadariyya, who claim souls are purified through acts of worship without God’s enabling.
rows.anchor: وفيه حجة على القدرية فإنهم زعموا أن طهارة النفوس بالطاعات والعبادات من غير توفيق من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears their words, including the slander and their expressed repentance, and knows their intentions; this urges sincere repentance.
rows.anchor: مبالغ في سمع الأقوال التي من جملتها ما قالوه من حديث الإفك وما أظهروه من التوبة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s many steps encompass every indecency and wrong, including slander, insults, lies, and searching out people’s faults.
rows.anchor: أن خطوات الشيطان كثيرة وهي جملة ما يطلق عليه الفحشاء والمنكر ومن جملته القذف والشتم والكذب وتفتيش عيوب الناس

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says human speech is against its speaker except speech commanding right, forbidding wrong, or remembering God.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "كلام ابن آدم كله عليه لاله إلا أمرا بمعروف

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith calls it great treachery to tell a brother something he trusts while lying to him.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "كثرت خيانة أن تحدث أخاك حديثا هو لك به مصدق وأنت له كاذب

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith praises the person whose own faults keep him occupied instead of other people’s faults.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "طوبى لمن شغله عيبه عن عيوب الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The practical counsel is to spend from lawful earnings, associate with jurists and wise people, and avoid the ignorant and sinful.
rows.anchor: وأنفق من مال اكتسبه من غير معصية وخالط أهل الفقه والحكمة وجانب أهل الجهل والمعصية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret Satan’s steps as vows to disobey God; vows to obey, such as prayer or fasting, are excluded because they prevent indecency and wrong.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم خطوات الشيطان النذور في معصية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification ultimately belongs to God, who enables obedience by grace, yet a student needs a teacher to learn purification according to God’s intent; the Prophet is the greatest means.
rows.anchor: أمر التزكية إنما هو إلى الله فإنه بفضله ورحمته وفق العبد للطاعات

rows.speaker: عبد الله الأنصاري
rows.claim: Abdullah al-Ansari says he had many hadith and law teachers, but Abu al-Hasan al-Kharaqani taught him the spiritual path; without meeting him, he would not have known reality.
rows.anchor: قال شيخ الإسلام عبد الله الأنصاري قدس سره : مشايخي في علم الحديث وعلم الشريعة

rows.speaker: عبد الله الأنصاري
rows.claim: Spiritual guides lead along the religious path and unlock certainty; the perfected human’s presence and companionship are a great blessing.
rows.anchor: فأهل الإرشاد هداة طريق الدين ومفاتيح أبواب اليقين فوجود الإنسان الكامل غنيمة ومجالسته نعمة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The absolute Light’s inward reality is, at the fullest realization, self-evident; none knows God except God.
rows.anchor: النور المطلق والمدلول باطنه وفي التحقيق الأتم هو دليل على نفسه لا يعرف الله إلا الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In houses” syntactically attaches to the later verb “is glorified.”
rows.anchor: متعلق بالفعل المذكور بعده وهو يسبح

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says bayt first meant a human’s night dwelling, then any dwelling; buyut usually means houses, abyat poetry, and the term also extends to a place where something is located.
rows.anchor: المفردات" : أصل البيت مأوى الإنسان بالليل ثم قد يقال من غير اعتبار الليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the houses as all mosques, God’s houses on earth that shine for heaven’s inhabitants as stars shine on earth.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالبيوت المساجد كلها لقول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض تضيء لأهل السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission means informing someone that a thing is allowed and granting leave for it.
rows.anchor: الإذن في الشيء إعلام بإجازته والرخصة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosques are to be raised by construction, reverence, and elevated rank.
rows.anchor: بالبناء أو التعظيم ورفع القدر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes raising physical objects, buildings, renown, and status, illustrating each sense with Qur’anic verses.
rows.anchor: الإمام الراغب : الرفع يقال تارة في الأجسام الموضوعة إذا أعليتها عن مقرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s name may denote His essence or an attribute of negation, affirmation, or action; it is general for every kind of remembrance, including tawhid, Qur’an, religious study, call to prayer, and its commencement.
rows.anchor: اسم الله تعالى ما يصح أن يطلق عليه بالنظر إلى ذاته أو باعتبار صفة من صفاته السلبية كالقدوس أو الثبوتية كالعليم

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars hold that divine names are restricted to names established by transmitted authority.
rows.anchor: لكنها توقيفية عند بعض العلماء وهو عام في كل ذكر توحيدا كان أو تلاوة قرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian gloss urges worshippers to occupy mosques with remembrance and prayer and avoid worldly or idle talk; an attributed report says mosque talk consumes good deeds like grazing animals consume grass.
rows.anchor: وفي الأثر : "الحديث في المسجد يأكل الحسنات كما تأكل البهيمة الحشيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “in them” emphasizes and recalls the preceding phrase across the intervening words; fronting it signals importance, not that glorification is confined to mosques.
rows.anchor: فيها تكرير لقوله في بيوت للتأكيد والتذكير لما بينهما من الفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih is declaring God’s transcendence; the word evokes swift movement through worship and extends to worship by speech, deed, or intention, here meaning the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: والتسبيح تنزيه الله وأصله المر السريع في عبادة الله فإن السبح المر السريع في الماء أو في الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specified times indicate obligatory prayers: ghuduww means the dawn prayer, while asal gathers the remaining prayers, as al-Kawashi explains.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالغدو وقت صلاة الفجر المؤداة بالغداة وبالآصال ما عداه من أوقات صلوات الظهر والعصر والعشاءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuduww is a verbal noun for entering morning time, between dawn prayer and sunrise; paired with asal, it is applied to the time itself.
rows.anchor: الغدو مصدر يقال : غدا يغدو غدوا أي دخل في وقت الغدوة وهي ما بين صلاة الغداة وطلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asal is the plural of asil, the evening period extending from the sun’s decline until dawn.
rows.anchor: جمع أصيل وهو العشي أي من زوال الشمس إلى طلوع الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijal is the subject of the verb yusabbihu.
rows.anchor: {رجال} فاعل يسبح {لا تلهيهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means nothing distracts them from their complete absorption in witnessing; the verb denotes diverting someone from what matters more.
rows.anchor: لا تشغلهم من غاية الاستغراق في مقام الشهود يقال : ألهاه عن كذا إذا شغله عما هو أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade refers to buying and selling; al-Mufradat defines it as deploying capital in pursuit of profit. It is singled out as their strongest and most familiar distraction, meaning no kind of trade distracts them.
rows.anchor: تخصيص التجارة لكونها أقوى الصوارف عندهم وأشهرها أي لا يشغلهم نوع من أنواع التجارة

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat defines trade as managing capital to seek profit and notes this is the only Arabic word with ta followed by jim.
rows.anchor: المفردات" : التجارة التصرف في رأس المال طالبا للربح وليس في كلامهم تاء بعدها جيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sale is giving the merchandise and receiving its price; purchase is giving the price and receiving the merchandise.
rows.anchor: البيع إعطاء المثمن وأخذ الثمن والشراء إعطاء الثمن وأخذ المثمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sale is named separately despite being included in trade because it is the more important of its two parts: profit is realized in a sale but only anticipated in a purchase, so if actual profit does not distract, potential profit will not.
rows.anchor: وإفراده بالذكر مع اندراجه تحت التجارة لكونه أهم من قسمي التجارة فإن الربح يتحقق بالبيع ويتوقع بالشراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God here means glorifying and praising Him.
rows.anchor: ذكر الله} بالتسبيح والتمجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it at its appointed times without delay.
rows.anchor: أي إقامتها بمواقيتها من غير تأخير وقد سقطت التاء المعوضة عن العين الساقطة بالإعلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compensatory ta is dropped after the weak radical is lost through sound change, with the genitive construction compensating for it.
rows.anchor: وقد سقطت التاء المعوضة عن العين الساقطة بالإعلال وعوض عنها الإضافة

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says establishing prayer requires observing all legally prescribed pillars, conditions, sunnas, and etiquettes; neglecting any means one has not established it.
rows.anchor: ابن الشيخ : إقامة الصلاة اتمامها برعاية جميع ما اعتبره الشرع من الأركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat is the wealth required to be given to eligible recipients; it is mentioned with prayer although not performed in mosques because the two commonly go together.
rows.anchor: أي : المال الذي فرض إخراجه للمستحقين وإيراده ههنا وإن لم يكن مما يفعل في البيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is expecting something disliked on a probable or certain indication; hope is expectation of something desired, and safety opposes fear.
rows.anchor: والخوف توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة أو معلومة كما أن الرجاء والطمع توقع محبوب عن أمارة مظنونة أو معلومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawman is the object of “they fear,” not an adverb of time, and refers to the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: مفعول ليخافون لا ظرف والمراد يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts and eyes undergo terror, changing and shifting: hearts rise to throats, as 33:10 says, and eyes stare fixedly, as 14:42 says.
rows.anchor: فتنقلب القلوب في الجوف وترتفع إلى الحنجرة ولا تنزل ولا تخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, hearts shift between hope of rescue and fear of destruction, while eyes scan where they will be taken or from which direction their records will arrive.
rows.anchor: أو تتقلب القلوب بين توقع النجاة وخوف الهلاك والأبصار من أي ناحية يؤخذ بهم ومن أي جهة يأتي كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase attaches to an omitted verb inferred from their praised deeds: they persist in remembrance, prayer, charity, and fear without distraction so God may reward them.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف يدل عليه ما حكي من أعمالهم المرضية أي يفعلون ما يفعلون من المداومة على التسبيح والذكر

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat distinguishes recompense, which can be good or bad, from ajr, which is reserved for good reward.
rows.anchor: والجزاء ما فيه الكفاية من المقابلة إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر والأجر خاص بالمثوبة الحسنى كما في "المفردات".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone, independently or jointly, owns sovereignty over the heavens and earth; mulk is authority to command and forbid among the people.
rows.anchor: له} خاصة دون غيره استقلالا أو اشتراكا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi glosses the phrase as God’s kingship over the heavens and earth, since He created them and is entitled to rule them.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ادشاهىء آسما نهارا وزمينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reply to Jews and Christians, God has no child to inherit His kingdom because He does not die.
rows.anchor: ردا على اليهود والنصارى : {ولم يتخذ ولدا} ليرث ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about not taking a child is coordinated with the preceding nominal clause.
rows.anchor: وهو عطف على ما قبله من الجملة الظرفية

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat derives ittakhadha from akhadha and says walad applies to singular or plural, young or old, male or female.
rows.anchor: المفردات" : تخذ بمعنى أخذ واتخذ افتعل منه والولد المولود

words: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reply to Quraysh, God has no partner in the heavens’ and earth’s sovereignty to contend with Him or assist in creating.
rows.anchor: ردا على قريش : {ولم يكن له شريك فى الملك} أي : في ملك السموات

words: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A couplet from the Mathnawi underscores that God alone rules His kingdom and that only a fool would call another His partner.
rows.anchor: واحد اندر ملك اورا يارنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought every existent thing into being from particular materials in specific forms, endowing it with diverse powers and properties and effects.
rows.anchor: أحدث كل موجود من الموجودات من مواد مخصوصة على صور معينة ورتب فيه قوى وخواص مختلفة الأحكام والآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fitted each thing to its intended properties and actions: humans can understand, reflect on worldly and next-worldly affairs, devise crafts, and perform varied work, as other kinds are fitted to their functions.
rows.anchor: فهيأه لما أراده منه من الخصائص والأفعال اللائقة به كهيئة الإنسان للإدراك والفهم والنظر والتدبر في أمور المعاش والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists take idols as gods besides the Creator, thereby turning away from worship of the one who made these things.
rows.anchor: أي حال كونهم متجاوزين عبادة الذي خلق هذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot create anything at all; they are described with rational-plural forms because the unbelievers treat them as rational beings, so the text addresses them in the unbelievers’ idiom, as Abu Layth notes.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر الأصنام بلفظ العقلاء لأن الكفار يجعلونهم بمنزلة العقلاء فخاطبهم بلغتهم كما في "تفسير أبي الليث"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi verses picture an attacker’s mockery turning back on him: one who tears others’ honor is himself exposed, then returns to Muhammad seeking pardon for ignorant ridicule.
rows.anchor: آنكه مي دريد جامه خلق ست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here lawla is an exhortation meaning “why not?” and tanzil is used without the sense of gradual descent, meaning “sent down,” so the wording does not contradict “all at once.”
rows.anchor: فلولا تحضيضية بمعنى هلا والتنزيل ههنا مجرد عن معنى التدريج بمعنى أنزل كخبر بمعنى أخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers ask for a single, simultaneous revelation, like the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
rows.anchor: واحدة} دفعة واحدة كالكتب الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection is bewildered and empty: inimitability is unaffected by gradual or complete revelation; they had been challenged to produce one sura and failed despite risking wealth and lives.
rows.anchor: وهذا اعتراض حيرة وبهت لا طائل تحته لأن الإعجاز لا يختلف بنزوله جملة أو مفرقا وقد تحدوا بسورة واحدة فعجزوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhalika is accusative as an adjective of an emphasized verbal noun, with the following clause giving its cause; it points back to the divided revelation they criticized.
rows.anchor: محل الكاف النصب على أنها صفة لمصدر مؤكد معلل بما بعده وذلك إشارة إلى ما يفهم من كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gradual revelation strengthens Muhammad’s heart by easing memorization, understanding, grasping rulings, and acting on them; each new revelation for an event increases strength and insight.
rows.anchor: لنقوي بذلك التنزيل المفرق فؤادك أي قلبك فإن فيه تيسيرا لحفظ النظم وفهم المعنى وضبط الأحكام والعمل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single bulk revelation made obedience difficult for the Israelites when the Torah descended all at once.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أن التوراة أنزلت دفعة فشق العمل على بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s gradual descent, a privilege particular to Muhammad among the prophets, lets his luminous heart take on the Qur’an’s character, grow strong in its light, and be nourished by its truths and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة إنزال القرآن منجما فضيلة خص بها نبينا عليه السلام من بين سائر النبيين فإن المقصود من إنزاله أن يتخلق قلبه المنير بخلق القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain spread over time nourishes crops better than a single downpour, illustrating why the Qur’an’s benefits are fulfilled through gradual revelation.
rows.anchor: ألا يرى أن الماء لو نزل من السماء جملة واحدة لما كانت تربية الزروع به مثلها إذا نزل مفرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We recited it distinctly” is coordinated with an elided verb expressing “We sent it down.”
rows.anchor: ورتلناه ترتيلا} عطف على ذلك المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartil means separating and placing each word after the last with a slight pause without cutting breath; its root image is the spacing of teeth.
rows.anchor: والترتيل التفريق ومجيء الكلمة بعد الأخرى بسكوت يسير دون قطع النفس وأصله في الأسنان وهو تفريجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent and recited it to Muhammad gradually, with calm and deliberation, over twenty or twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: كذلك نزلناه وقرأناه عليك شيئا بعد شيء على تؤدة وتمهل في عشرين سنة أو ثلاث وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They bring no strange question or speech, likened to a false example, intended to disparage Muhammad or the Qur’an, without God bringing a response.
rows.anchor: أي بسؤال عجيب وكلام غريب كأنه مثل في البطلان يريدون به القدح في حقك وحق القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers their challenge with truth: the bāʾ also marks transitivity, and the true answer invalidates their claim and ends the dispute.
rows.anchor: فالباء في قوله : {بالحق} للتعدية أيضا أي بالجواب الحق الثابت المبطل لما جاؤوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes night cover people with darkness like clothing; labs means covering, and the Qur’an similarly calls spouses garments for each other and piety a garment by analogy.
rows.anchor: كاللباس يستركم بظلامه كما يستر اللباس فشبه ظلامه باللباس في الستر وأصل اللبس ستر الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night’s darkness does not remove the prayer requirement to cover one’s nakedness; that requirement remains in darkness and light.
rows.anchor: لا اعتبار لستر الظلمة فإن ستر العورة باللباس ونحوه لحق الصلاة وهو باق في الظلمة والضوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep is relaxation of the brain’s nerves due to rising moist vapor; sabt means stopping work, and Saturday is named for that stoppage, or for ending the days after six days of creation.
rows.anchor: النوم استرخاء أعصاب الدماغ برطوبات البخار الصاعد والسبت قطع العمل ويوم سبتهم يوم قطعهم للعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep, usually at night, rests the body by interrupting waking occupations; alternatively, sleep is called death because both share a severing of life, as 6:60 says God takes people at night.
rows.anchor: وجعل النوم الذي يقع في الليل غالبا راحة للأبدان بقطع المشاغل والأعمال المختصة بحال اليقظة أو جعله موتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death wholly separates the spirit’s light from the body, while sleep separates it only from the body’s exterior, not its interior; masbut can mean dead or unconscious, so such patients should not be buried before a day and night confirms death.
rows.anchor: أن الموت هو الانقطاع الكلي أي انقطاع ضوء الروح عن ظاهر البدن وباطنه
